finding.claim: The icon value passed to Profile.update() is stored without validation and later used as the target of a server-side GET in the nightly sync() job, enabling blind SSRF to any http/https host reachable from the job.
finding.source: Profile.update(String webhook, String icon) parameter icon (src/Profile.java:11), presumed attacker-controlled via the PUT /profile handler (handler not in repo).

trace.note: Regex validation applies only to webhook, not icon
this.iconUrl = icon stores the value unchecked
c.send GET issued server-side to attacker-chosen URL; response body buffered via ofByteArray and discarded

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host, port, or private/loopback/link-local address check on icon; no allowlist; URI.create is syntax-only. Java HttpClient rejects non-http(s) schemes so file: is not reachable. Redirect policy depends on the injected HttpClient (JDK default is NEVER); if it follows redirects, a public URL can redirect into internal space and no re-validation exists. Response is discarded, so the attack is blind (internal reachability and side effects only). Severity Medium; High if the job can reach cloud metadata or internal services. Assumes PUT /profile handler passes icon from user input without other checks (not in repo).

verdict.guard_found: none. Line 12 validates only `webhook`, and `icon` goes straight to `this.iconUrl` at line 16 with no scheme, host, or private-address check. The sync() job then calls `URI.create(iconUrl)` and sends a GET at lines 23-24.
verdict.reason: Every trace line checks out (src/Profile.java:11, 12, 16, 20, 23-24), and no guard exists on `icon`, but the source is unproven: the only caller is the PUT /profile handler, which is not in the repo (src/Profile.java:10-11), so I cannot confirm that `icon` is attacker-controlled rather than admin-set or validated upstream.
